 Florida CFO confirms all fraudulently issued driver’s licenses have been revoked following Broward DMV arrest 
 Florida News 
 By Michelle Vecerina 
 Published Nov. 19, 2026, 12:18 p.m. ET | Updated Nov. 19, 2026
 Pembroke Pines driver’s license examiner Lynnette Stitt Williams arrested on 360 felony counts. (Photo/Broward County Crime Watch Facebook) 
 FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. — Florida Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia confirmed that every driver’s license unlawfully issued to individuals lacking legal status through an alleged Broward County licensing fraud scheme has been revoked, following calls from U.S. Rep. Greg Steube for a full audit of the credentials.
 Ingoglia, a Republican, initially announced on X that he had contacted the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles to ensure “every single one of these illegal alien licenses are revoked” following the arrest of Pembroke Pines driver’s license examiner Lynnette Stitt Williams on 360 felony counts.
 In a follow-up post on X, Ingoglia confirmed the revocations had been completed.
 “CONFIRMED. All the licenses given to illegals have been REVOKED,” Ingoglia wrote.
 CONFIRMED. All the licenses given to illegals have been REVOKED.
— Blaise Ingoglia (@GovGoneWild) November 18, 2026 
 The action came alongside demands from Steube who urged state leaders to audit the system and revoke every license obtained illegally, while criticizing a judge’s courtroom remark during Stitt Williams’ bond hearing.
 “Anyone I know would get sent home over a missing document at the DMV,” Steube wrote. “In Broward, investigators say people could pay a driving school to get around the rules. The judge’s response? ‘We all make mistakes.’ Audit the licenses and revoke every one that was issued illegally.”
 According to court records and local reporting from NBC 6 South Florida and CBS News Miami, Florida Highway Patrol troopers arrested Stitt Williams on 360 felony charges tied to 60 allegedly fraudulent credentials. Investigators alleged applicants paid a driving school to guarantee licenses regardless of legal status, bypassing standard appointment and testing requirements.
 The charges include 60 counts each of unauthorized possession or display of a driver’s license, unlawful issuance of a driver’s license, supplying or aiding in supplying an unauthorized driver’s license, forgery, criminal use of a public record or providing false information, and official misconduct.
 Investigators wrote in an arrest affidavit that applicants were routed directly to Stitt Williams, with some applications listing false residential addresses and multiple applicants submitting identical utility and cable bills as proof of Florida residency. Authorities also alleged licenses were issued to individuals who had not passed required driving exams.
 During Stitt Williams’ initial court appearance in Broward County, Judge Allison Gilman found probable cause for the charges and set bond at $15,000, declining prosecutors’ request for a $900,000 bond.
 The arrest came days after Florida Highway Patrol troopers arrested a separate former Broward County driver’s license examiner in Sunrise on 77 felony charges, including racketeering, in an unrelated identity-theft licensing investigation.
 In a letter dated Thursday to Florida Secretary of State Cord Byrd, Ingoglia also asked the Department of State’s Division of Elections to conduct a comprehensive review to determine whether any recipients of the fraudulently issued licenses registered or cast ballots in Florida elections.
 “Today I sent this letter to @FLSecofState asking for a comprehensive review to find out if the illegal immigrants who unlawfully obtained drivers licenses registered and/or voted in our elections,” Ingoglia wrote on X. “If any of them did, they should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Protecting the integrity of our elections has always been, and will remain, a top priority in Florida.”
 In the letter, Ingoglia requested that election officials cross-check individuals tied to the scheme against Florida’s statewide voter registration database in coordination with the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles, the Broward County Supervisor of Elections and federal agencies . He also asked officials to review whether any of the individuals submitted voter applications, requested vote-by-mail ballots or cast ballots in any federal, state or local election, refer credible violations for prosecution and release a public summary of the findings .
 Today I sent this letter to @FLSecofState asking for a comprehensive review to find out if the illegal immigrants who unlawfully obtained drivers licenses registered and/or voted in our elections. 
If any of them did, they should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. 
Protecting the integrity of our elections has always been, and will remain, a top priority in Florida.
— Blaise Ingoglia (@GovGoneWild) November 19, 2026 
 Editor’s note: This story has been updated to include Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia’s Nov. 19 letter to Florida Secretary of State Cord Byrd requesting a comprehensive voter registration and election review.
